items.question: What is the minimum GPA required to qualify for the BSSE degree?
items.ground_truth_answer: A Grade Point Average of 2.5 or above.

items.question: List all the requirements a student must meet to qualify for the BSSE degree.
items.ground_truth_answer: Complete minimum 144 credits including an internship; minimum grade C+ in the Comprehensive Examination; pass every course individually with at least D; GPA of 2.5 or above.
key_facts: at least D in every course
items.notes: The 144 figure conflicts with 150 elsewhere; see CONFLICT category.

items.question: How many credits must a student register for in each semester?
items.ground_truth_answer: 18 credits per semester. A student who fails to take 18 credits in a regular semester stands withdrawn for that semester, unless the IIT academic committee grants an exception.
key_facts: exception by academic committee of IIT
items.notes: Year 1 terms list 21 credits; see CONFLICT-002.

items.question: What happens if I take fewer than 18 credits in a regular semester?
items.ground_truth_answer: You stand withdrawn from the program for that semester; only the academic committee of IIT can make an exception.
key_facts: exception only by academic committee of IIT

items.question: Who is allowed a relaxed (lighter) course load?
items.ground_truth_answer: Transfer students, and students who are enrolling again after withdrawal.

items.question: Below what attendance percentage is a student treated as non-collegiate?
items.ground_truth_answer: Less than 75% attendance.

items.question: How can a non-collegiate student still sit for the exam and what does it cost?
items.ground_truth_answer: Apply to the Director, Regular Program Office; with approval of the IIT academic committee the student deposits TK. 3000/- as a fine per university rules.
key_facts: apply to Director, Regular Program Office

items.question: What is the minimum attendance below which a student cannot sit for the exam at all?
items.ground_truth_answer: Below 60% attendance a student should not be allowed to sit for the examination.
key_facts: not allowed to sit for exam

items.question: My attendance is 68%. Can I still take the semester final exam?
items.ground_truth_answer: Yes, but as a non-collegiate student (below 75%): you must apply to the Director, Regular Program Office, get academic committee approval and pay a TK 3000 fine. 68% is above the 60% cutoff.
key_facts: must apply, get approval, pay TK 3000

items.question: My attendance is 55%. Can I sit for the final exam?
items.ground_truth_answer: No. Below 60% attendance a student should not be allowed to sit for the examination under university rules.

items.question: How many weeks of scheduled classes are there in a semester?
items.ground_truth_answer: 14 weeks.

items.question: Give the full breakdown of a semester by weeks.
items.ground_truth_answer: 14 weeks scheduled classes; 1 week exam preparation; 3 weeks semester final examination; 3 weeks result publication; 4 weeks vacation and holidays; 1 week supplementary examinations.

items.question: How many weeks does a whole semester cycle add up to?
items.ground_truth_answer: 26 weeks (14+1+3+3+4+1), roughly the stated six months.

items.question: How many semesters does the BSSE program have?
items.ground_truth_answer: Eight semesters over four years, each about six months long.

items.question: How many hours per week is one theory credit and one lab credit?
items.ground_truth_answer: One theory credit is 1 hour per week; one lab credit is 2 hours per week.

items.question: How many contact hours per week does a 3-credit lab course need?
items.ground_truth_answer: 6 hours per week (3 credits x 2 hours per lab credit).
items.notes: Example: SE 2112 Software Project Lab I is 3 lab credits.

items.question: What CGPA must a student have to be promoted to the next semester?
items.ground_truth_answer: The overall CGPA of the previous semester must not be less than 2.5, and the student must get at least D in each course.
key_facts: at least D in each course

items.question: My CGPA is 2.8 but I got an F in one course. What happens?
items.ground_truth_answer: You sit for a supplementary exam in that course and can receive no more than B+.

items.question: What if a student fails to get promoted?
items.ground_truth_answer: They retake that semester with the following batch, and may retake only the courses in which they got an F.

items.question: Is the Comprehensive Examination grade counted in the CGPA?
items.ground_truth_answer: No. It is shown on the Grade Sheet but not included in the CGPA calculation.

items.question: What is the minimum grade needed in the Comprehensive Examination, and when is it taken?
items.ground_truth_answer: A minimum grade of C+. It is usually taken two weeks before the end of the final semester.
key_facts: two weeks before end of final semester

items.question: Can I retake the Comprehensive Examination if I fail?
items.ground_truth_answer: Yes, but only once, unless the Academic Committee decides otherwise.

items.question: What does the Comprehensive Examination test?
items.ground_truth_answer: The student's understanding of their major areas of study, i.e. the Software Engineering courses.

items.question: Does a grade of C satisfy the Comprehensive Examination requirement?
items.ground_truth_answer: No. The exam needs at least C+ (2.50); C is 2.25 and is below that.

items.question: What is the penalty for using unfair means in exams?
items.ground_truth_answer: Students who adopt unfair means are punished according to the rules of Noakhali Science and Technology University.

items.question: When do students do the internship and what must they do afterwards?
items.ground_truth_answer: In the seventh semester (Year 4 Term 1) they are placed with a well-known IT organization; on return they present a report on their domain of work and are also evaluated by the organization.

items.question: How is the SE 4100 Internship graded?
items.ground_truth_answer: Using marks provided by the company along with the marks of at least two presentations given at IIT. It is full-time for six months and worth 18 credits.
key_facts: at least two presentations at IIT

items.question: Can the institute change the curriculum without telling students?
items.ground_truth_answer: Yes. IIT reserves the right to change the program, courses and statements at any time without notice, and NSTU/IIT bear no responsibility for resulting adjustments or expenses.
key_facts: changes at any time without notice
no responsibility for adjustments or expenses

items.question: What is the lowest grade that counts as passing a course?
items.ground_truth_answer: D (2.00, marks 40% to below 45%) is the lowest passing grade; below 40% is F.

items.question: Why must I get a supplementary exam if I fail but my CGPA is fine, and what is the best grade I can get?
items.ground_truth_answer: Students with CGPA of 2.5 but an F in a course sit a supplementary exam; the best grade is B+.

items.question: What grade point does an A grade carry?
items.ground_truth_answer: 3.75 (marks 75% to below 80%, 'Better').

items.question: What marks range gives a B+?
items.ground_truth_answer: 65% or above but below 70%, grade point 3.25 ('Above average').

items.question: What marks do I need for A+?
items.ground_truth_answer: 80% or above (grade point 4.00, 'Excellent').

items.question: I scored 52% in a course. What letter grade and grade point is that?
items.ground_truth_answer: C+ with grade point 2.50 ('Satisfactory').

items.question: I scored 44%. Did I pass?
items.ground_truth_answer: Yes. 40% to below 45% is D (2.00, 'Pass').

items.question: I scored 39%. What is my result?
items.ground_truth_answer: F (0.00, Fail), since below 40% is F.

items.question: Which grade is described as 'Not satisfactory'?
items.ground_truth_answer: C, grade point 2.25, marks 45% to below 50%.

items.question: What do the grade codes I and W mean?
items.ground_truth_answer: I means Incomplete and W means Withdrawn.

items.question: What grade corresponds to marks from 55% to 59%?
items.ground_truth_answer: B- with grade point 2.75 ('Below average'). The source row is typo'd as '>=55% but 60%', meant to be '<60%'.

items.question: In which year and term is Software Testing and Quality Assurance taught?

items.question: When do students take Computer Networks?

items.question: Which Year 2 Term 1 entries are lab courses?
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2102, SE 2104, CSE 2106, MATH 2108, SE 2110 (the labs of the five theory courses) and SE 2112 Software Project Lab I.

items.question: How many electives does a student take, and in which term?

items.question: How many credits does the Project (SE 4202) carry and in which term?

items.question: Is Artificial Intelligence taught in the third year?

items.question: What are the recommended books for Software Testing and Quality Assurance?
items.ground_truth_answer: Naresh Chauhan, Software Testing: Principles and Practices; Myers, Sandler and Badgett, The Art of Software Testing; Crispin and Gregory, Agile Testing.

items.question: What are the references for Software Metrics?
items.ground_truth_answer: Fenton and Bieman, Software Metrics: A Rigorous and Practical Approach (3rd ed.); Laird and Brennan, Software Measurement and Estimation: A Practical Approach (1st ed.).

items.question: Which textbook does Information Security use?
items.ground_truth_answer: Information Security: Principles and Practice by Mark Stamp, 2nd edition, Wiley 2011.

items.question: What is covered in the Theory of Computation course?
items.ground_truth_answer: Mathematical background; finite automata and regular expressions (DFA/NFA, Kleene's theorem); properties of regular sets (pumping lemma); context-free grammars and languages; simplified/normal forms (Chomsky); pushdown automata; and an introduction to Turing machines.

items.question: What does the Web Technology course say about web security?
items.ground_truth_answer: It covers Denial of Service, Buffer Overflow, Cross Site Scripting, and Authentication and Access Control.

items.question: Which programming language is taught in Object Oriented Concepts I?
items.ground_truth_answer: Java (JVM/JRE/JDK, syntax, string operations, I/O, exception handling, logging and debugging).

items.question: What does Structured Programming cover and how many credits is it?
items.ground_truth_answer: C programming: control statements, data types, variables, expressions, arrays and strings, pointers and functions, console and file I/O, structures and unions. 3 credits in total (1 theory + 2 lab; the lab is CSE 1102).

items.question: How many credits is Computer Networks including its lab?
items.ground_truth_answer: 3 credits: CSE 2105 theory (2) + CSE 2106 lab (1).

items.question: Which topics does the Data Structure course include?
items.ground_truth_answer: Complexity, searching (linear/binary), sorting (insertion, selection, bubble, quick, merge, radix), recursion, linked lists, stacks and queues, hashing, trees (BST, heaps, AVL, B and B+), graphs (BFS, DFS, shortest path, MST, topological sort), and problem-solving strategies (greedy, divide and conquer, DP, backtracking).

items.question: How is Software Project Lab II organised?
items.ground_truth_answer: Students form project teams of 3 (variable for special cases, decided by the course manager); each team first prepares its Software Requirements Specification (SRS), then develops the project.

items.question: Is Software Project Lab I a group or an individual project?
items.ground_truth_answer: Individual: each student completes the software project separately and is marked on their own software, which should demand significant problem solving.

items.question: What deliverables are required for the SE 4202 software development project?
items.ground_truth_answer: Project proposal, Software Requirements Specification, Software Design Specification, Software Test Plan and User Manual, plus multiple intermediate presentations. A research project requires a thesis instead.

items.question: How does the SRS and Analysis lab assign work?
items.ground_truth_answer: One small real-life system is analysed by everyone in class; three real-life mid-scale systems are distributed among randomly formed groups of 5/6 students (one project per group). Output is specification reports.
items.notes: SE 2210 lab is NOT merged into SE 2209 by the chunker (different content).

items.question: What tools are used in the Software Testing course?
items.ground_truth_answer: JUnit, Selenium, Apache JMeter, Sprajax, Sqlninja, Bugzilla and Cucumber; class projects are in groups of at most 3.

items.question: What topics does the Algorithm Analysis course cover?
items.ground_truth_answer: Greedy algorithms, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, graph searching and shortest paths, linear programming, selected topics (computational geometry, number theoretic and string matching) and NP-completeness/approximation algorithms.

items.question: What are the Operating Systems course references?
items.ground_truth_answer: Operating System Concepts, 7th ed., Silberschatz/Galvin/Gagne; Modern Operating Systems, 4th ed., Tanenbaum and Bos.

items.question: What does Business Studies for Engineers cover?
items.ground_truth_answer: Management and entrepreneurship, organization theory, strategic management; accounting basics (accounting equation, journal, adjusting and closing entries, financial statements); and financial statement analysis including ratio analysis.

items.question: Which suggested reading in Software Security is Aleph One's article?
items.ground_truth_answer: 'Smashing the Stack for Fun and Profit' (Phrack Vol 7, Nr. 49).
key_facts: Smashing the Stack for Fun and Profit

items.question: What is the Information Retrieval elective about and which books does it use?
items.ground_truth_answer: Boolean retrieval/inverted index, tokenization, tolerant retrieval, index construction, scoring (tf-idf, vector space), evaluation, relevance feedback and Apache Lucene. Books: Manning/Raghavan/Schutze An Introduction to Information Retrieval; McCandless et al. Lucene in Action. 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab).

items.question: Which textbook does Applied Data Science use?
items.ground_truth_answer: Mount and Zumel (2014), Practical Data Science with R.

items.question: What book is used for Distributed Systems?
items.ground_truth_answer: Distributed Systems: Concepts and Design (5th edition) by Coulouris, Dollimore, Kindberg and Blair.

items.question: What does GE 1209 History of Emergence of Bangladesh cover?
items.ground_truth_answer: Partition of Bengal 1905 and its annulment 1911; 1947 partition, Pakistan's structure and disparity, the Language Movement, Ayub-Yahia rule; the Six Point and 11-Point movements, Agartala Case, 1969 upsurge; the 1970 election, March 1971 non-cooperation, declaration of independence and the formation of the government.

items.question: What topics are in Professional Ethics for Information Systems?
items.ground_truth_answer: Ethics, morals, integrity; ethics for IT workers and users (whistle blowing, bribery, code of ethics); computer and internet crime; privacy; freedom of expression; intellectual property; impact of IT on society; social networking issues. Book: George W. Reynolds, Ethics in Information Technology.

items.question: What reference books are listed for Software Project Management?
items.ground_truth_answer: Stellman and Greene, Applied Software Project Management; Phillips, IT Project Management: On Track from Start to Finish; Rubin, Essential Scrum.

items.question: What is the Software Maintenance course about?
items.ground_truth_answer: Lifecycle roadmap of evolution and maintenance; evolution laws; pre-delivery and transition models; impact analysis; handling customer problems; retirement; maintainability vs bad smells; refactoring; legacy system evolution; architectural patterns for isolating change.

items.question: What book is used for Business Psychology?
items.ground_truth_answer: Industrial and Organizational Psychology: Research and Practice, 5th edition, by Paul E. Spector.

items.question: What credits split does Management Information Systems (BUS 602) have and which book does it use?

items.question: What does the Computer Graphics and Multimedia elective teach?
items.ground_truth_answer: OpenGL, color models, geometric transformations, 3D viewing, ray tracing, Phong shading, rasterization (Bresenham), hidden surface removal, texture mapping; reference Foley, van Dam, Feiner and Hughes. 3 credits.

items.question: Can I eat or smoke in the computer lab?

items.question: Give me the course details of Structured Programming.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 1101 Structured Programming - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab; lab course CSE 1102). Outline: C programming fundamentals: control statements, data types, variables and expressions, arrays and strings, pointers and functions, console and file I/O, structures and unions. References: Herbert Schildt: Teach Yourself C and C: The Complete Reference (McGraw Hill); Schaum's Outline of Programming with C.

items.question: Details of CSE 1103
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 1103 Discrete Mathematics - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Logic and proofs; sets, functions, sequences and matrices; number theory; induction and recursion; counting; relations; graphs; trees. References: Kenneth H. Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and its Applications, 7th ed.

items.question: Tell me everything about the Probability and Statistics for Engineers-I course.
items.ground_truth_answer: STAT 1105 Probability and Statistics for Engineers-I - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Descriptive statistics; elements of probability and Bayes' theorem; random variables and expectation; special distributions; sampling distributions and the Central Limit Theorem; parameter estimation. References: Sheldon M. Ross, Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists (3rd ed.); M. Nurul Islam, An Introduction to Statistics and Probability; Lipschutz, 2000 Solved Problems in Discrete Mathematics.

items.question: What is Calculus and Analytical Geometry about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: MATH 1107 Calculus and Analytical Geometry - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Limits, series and basic concepts; differential calculus; integral calculus; linear algebra and vector calculus (matrices, determinants, eigenvalue problems). References: G. B. Thomas and R. L. Finney, Calculus and Analytical Geometry (9th ed.); Erwin Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics (9th ed.).

items.question: Give me the course details of Soft Skill Communication.
items.ground_truth_answer: GE 1109 Soft Skill Communication - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Elements and process of communication; verbal and non-verbal communication and body language; general versus business communication; sounds of English; English grammar review. References: B. K. Das et al., An Introduction to Professional English and Soft Skills (Cambridge); Raman and Sharma, Technical Communication; Rizvi, Effective Technical Communication; Alan Pease, Understanding Body Language; plus further grammar and pronunciation books.

items.question: Details of GE 1111
items.ground_truth_answer: GE 1111 Technology and Society - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course GE 1112). Outline: Nature of technology, social forces that affect its adoption, impact on society, innovation, and public policy implications of changing technology. References: Society and Technological Change, 6th ed. (Worth Publishers).

items.question: Tell me everything about the Introduction to Software Engineering course.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 1113 Introduction to Software Engineering - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Introduction to computers, basic computer organization, processor and memory, storage and I/O devices, software, software engineering and software process models. References: Pradip K. Sinha, Computer Fundamentals (BPB); Pressman, Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach, 7th ed.

items.question: What is Data Structure about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 1201 Data Structure - Year 1 Term 2; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab; lab course CSE 1202). Outline: Complexity and searching; sorting (insertion, selection, bubble, quick, merge, radix) and recursion; linked lists; stacks and queues with prefix/infix/postfix evaluation; hashing; trees (binary, BST, heaps, Huffman, AVL, B and B+); graphs (BFS, DFS, shortest paths, MST, topological sort); greedy, divide and conquer, dynamic programming and backtracking. References: Schaum's Outline: Data Structures; Horowitz and Sahni, Fundamentals of Data Structures; Robert Kruse, Data Structures and Program Design (2nd ed.).

items.question: Give me the course details of Computer Organization.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 1203 Computer Organization - Year 1 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 1204). Outline: Function and structure of a computer; number representation and arithmetic; digital logic and integrated circuits; instruction representation and assembly language (CISC/RISC); processing and control unit; memory subsystem including cache and virtual memory; I/O subsystem; multiprocessing. References: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design; Hamacher, Vranesic and Zaky, Computer Organization; Stallings, Computer Organization and Architecture; Hayes, Computer Architecture and Organization.

items.question: Details of STAT 1205
items.ground_truth_answer: STAT 1205 Probability and Statistics for Engineers-II - Year 1 Term 2; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Hypothesis testing; regression and correlation analysis; analysis of variance; goodness-of-fit and categorical data analysis; nonparametric tests; quality control charts. References: Ross (3rd ed.); Montgomery and Runger, Applied Statistics and Probability for Engineers (4th ed.); Spiegel, Schiller and Srinivasan, Schaum's Outline: Probability and Statistics (3rd ed.).

items.question: Tell me everything about the Ordinary Differential Equations course.
items.ground_truth_answer: MATH 1207 Ordinary Differential Equations - Year 1 Term 2; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Mathematical modelling and first-order ODEs (separable, exact, linear, Bernoulli); second-order and higher-order linear equations; existence and uniqueness; systems of ODEs, critical points and stability; Laplace transforms. References: Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics (8th ed.); S. L. Ross, Differential Equations; Coddington, An Introduction to Ordinary Differential Equations; Tenenbaum and Pollard, Ordinary Differential Equations.

items.question: What is History of Emergence of Bangladesh about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: GE 1209 History of Emergence of Bangladesh - Year 1 Term 2; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Partition of Bengal (1905) and its annulment (1911); 1947 partition, Pakistan's structure, disparity and the Language Movement; Ayub-Yahia rule; the Six Point and 11-Point movements, Agartala Case and 1969 upsurge; the 1970 election, March 1971 non-cooperation, declaration of independence and formation of the Bangladesh government. References: Harun-or-Rashid, Foreshadowing of Bangladesh, plus six Bengali-language references whose text is garbled in the source.

items.question: Give me the course details of Object Oriented Concepts I.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 1213 Object Oriented Concepts I - Year 1 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 1214). Outline: Object-oriented concepts (objects, classes, UML class diagrams, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, composition); constructors and class design guidelines; designing with objects; frameworks and reuse. Programming lessons in Java: JVM/JDK, syntax, strings, I/O, exception handling, logging and debugging. References: Matt Weisfeld, The Object Oriented Thought Process; Deitel and Deitel, Java How to Program; Herbert Schildt, Java: The Complete Reference.

items.question: Details of CSE 2101
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2101 Algorithm Analysis - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2102). Outline: Designing and analysing algorithms; greedy algorithms; divide and conquer; dynamic programming; graph searching and shortest paths; linear programming; selected topics (computational geometry, number-theoretic and string matching); NP-completeness and approximation algorithms. References: Cormen et al., Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press; the handbook misspells the first author 'Corman'); Aho, Hopcroft and Ullman, The Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms.

items.question: Tell me everything about the Theory of Computation course.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 2103 Theory of Computation - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 2104). Outline: Mathematical background; finite automata and regular expressions; properties of regular sets (pumping lemma); context-free grammars and languages; normal forms (Chomsky); pushdown automata; introduction to Turing machines. References: Hopcroft, Motwani and Ullman, Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation, 3rd ed.

items.question: What is Computer Networks about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2105 Computer Networks - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2106). Outline: Overview of the Internet and protocol layers; application layer (HTTP, FTP, e-mail, DNS); transport layer (UDP, TCP, congestion control); network layer (IP, subnetting, link-state and distance-vector routing, RIP, OSPF, BGP). References: B. A. Forouzan, Data Communications and Networking, 5th ed.

items.question: Give me the course details of Numerical Analysis for Engineers.
items.ground_truth_answer: MATH 2107 Numerical Analysis for Engineers - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course MATH 2108). Outline: Calculus review and C programming; sources and propagation of errors; root finding for nonlinear equations; systems of linear equations; interpolation and approximation; numerical integration and differentiation. References: E. Balagurusamy, Numerical Methods (Tata McGraw-Hill, 2002).

items.question: Details of SE 2109
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 2109 Object Oriented Concepts II - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 2110). Outline: Composition and building objects; object models with UML; XML and portable data; persistence; objects and the Internet; client/server applications; OO design principles (SOLID); component-based design, design patterns and code smells. Java: generics, collections, reflection, multithreading, Swing, serialization, sockets, servlets, JavaBeans. References: Weisfeld; Deitel and Deitel; Schildt; Sierra and Bates, Head First Java.

items.question: Tell me everything about the Software Project Lab I course.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 2112 Software Project Lab I - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (lab/practical). Outline: An individual software project: each student completes a project separately, is marked on their own software, and should show skills from earlier courses through significant problem-solving effort. References: No references listed.

items.question: What is Operating Systems and System Programming about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2201 Operating Systems and System Programming - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2202). Outline: Processes, threads, IPC and scheduling; memory management and virtual memory; file systems; I/O; deadlocks; virtualization and cloud. References: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 7th ed.; Tanenbaum and Bos, Modern Operating Systems, 4th ed.

items.question: Give me the course details of Business Psychology.
items.ground_truth_answer: GE 2203 Business Psychology - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Fundamentals of psychology in business; job analysis; selection and placement tests; training and development; motivation theories; job attitudes and emotion; productive and counterproductive behaviour; occupational health; leadership; organizational development and theory. References: Paul E. Spector, Industrial and Organizational Psychology: Research and Practice, 5th ed. (numbered '3.' in the source).

items.question: Details of CSE 2205
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2205 Information Security - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2206). Outline: Security concepts and attacks; classical encryption; block ciphers and DES; public-key cryptography (RSA, Diffie-Hellman); hash functions, MACs and digital signatures; key management and X.509; network and internet security (TLS, WLAN, e-mail). References: Mark Stamp, Information Security: Principles and Practice, 2nd ed. (Wiley, 2011).

items.question: Tell me everything about the Database Management System-I course.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2207 Database Management System-I - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2208). Outline: Introduction to database systems; ER data modelling; relational model and normalization; SQL; overview of object-oriented databases and persistence. References: Silberschatz, Korth and Sudarshan, Database System Concepts, 6th ed.

items.question: What is Software Requirements Spec. and Analysis about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 2209 Software Requirements Spec. and Analysis - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 2210). Outline: Review of software process models; requirements engineering (elicitation, negotiation, validation); requirements analysis and modelling (scenario-based, UML, data, class-based, flow-oriented, behavioural). References: Pressman, Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach (7th ed. or higher); Sommerville, Software Engineering (9th ed. or higher).

items.question: Give me the course details of Business Studies for Engineers.
items.ground_truth_answer: BUS 2211 Business Studies for Engineers - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Management and entrepreneurship; organization theory; strategic management; accounting basics (accounting equation, journal, adjusting and closing entries, financial statements); financial statement analysis and ratio analysis. References: Robbins and Coulter, Management; Weygandt, Kieso and Kimmel, Accounting Principles, 8th ed.

items.question: Details of SE 3101
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3101 Professional Ethics for Information Systems - Year 3 Term 1; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Ethics, morals and integrity; ethics for IT workers and users (whistle blowing, bribery, codes of ethics); computer and internet crime; privacy; freedom of expression; intellectual property; impact of IT on society. References: George W. Reynolds, Ethics in Information Technology.

items.question: Tell me everything about the Web Technology course.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 3103 Web Technology - Year 3 Term 1; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab; lab course CSE 3104). Outline: HTML, JavaScript and CSS; server-side programming (HTTP and application servers, MVC frameworks, web services); database access (ORM, LINQ); web security (DoS, buffer overflow, XSS, authentication and access control). References: Deitel et al., Internet and World Wide Web: How to Program; Rajkamal, Web Technology; Bayross, Teach Yourself Web Technologies; Niederst, Web Design in a Nutshell.

items.question: What is Data Science and Analytics – DBMS II about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 3105 Data Science and Analytics – DBMS II - Year 3 Term 1; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab; lab course CSE 3106). Outline: Indexing and hashing; query processing and optimization; transactions, concurrency control and recovery; data analysis and mining; database architectures; parallel and distributed databases. References: Elmasri and Navathe, Fundamentals of Database Systems; Garcia-Molina, Ullman and Widom, Database Systems: The Complete Book; Silberschatz, Korth and Sudarshan, Database System Concepts, 5th ed.

items.question: Give me the course details of Business Communication.
items.ground_truth_answer: BUS 3107 Business Communication - Year 3 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course BUS 3108). Outline: Role of communication in business; business writing; message patterns (direct, indirect, persuasive); letters, memos and e-mail; job-search activities (CV writing, interviews); report writing; other forms of business communication. References: Lesikar, Pettit and Flatley, Lesikar's Basic Business Communication (McGraw Hill).

items.question: Details of SE 3109
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3109 Design Pattern - Year 3 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 3110). Outline: Types of design patterns (creational, behavioural, structural); code smells and refactoring; SOLID design principles. References: Gamma et al., Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software (Pearson, 1995).

items.question: Tell me everything about the Software Project Lab II course.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3112 Software Project Lab II - Year 3 Term 1; 3 credits (lab/practical). Outline: Team-based project: teams of 3 (variable for special cases, decided by the course manager); each team prepares a Software Requirements Specification (SRS) first and then develops the project. References: No references listed.

items.question: What is Distributed Systems about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 3201 Distributed Systems - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab; lab course CSE 3202). Outline: Characterization and system models; interprocess communication and remote invocation; middleware (distributed objects, web services, peer-to-peer); distributed file and name services; time, coordination and agreement; transactions and replication; mobile and ubiquitous computing. References: Coulouris, Dollimore, Kindberg and Blair, Distributed Systems: Concepts and Design, 5th ed.
items.notes: Lab is a separate chunk in the index (different content).

items.question: Give me the course details of Software Metrics.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3203 Software Metrics - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 3204). Outline: Basics of measurement; goal-based framework; empirical investigation; measuring size, structure, cost and effort, quality and reliability; object-oriented metrics; hands-on implementation and comparison with industry tools. References: Fenton and Bieman, Software Metrics: A Rigorous and Practical Approach, 3rd ed.; Laird and Brennan, Software Measurement and Estimation, 1st ed.

items.question: Details of SE 3205
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3205 Software Security - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 3206). Outline: Security principles and policies; security risks (database, operating system, secure coding); countermeasures and vulnerability elimination; secure software design guidelines and standards. References: Pfleeger, Security in Computing, 4th ed.; Stallings and Brown, Computer Security; Chess and West, Secure Programming with Static Analysis; Wheeler, Secure Programming HOWTO; Goertzel et al.; Aleph One, Smashing the Stack for Fun and Profit; Newsham, Format String Attacks.

items.question: Tell me everything about the Artificial Intelligence course.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 3207 Artificial Intelligence - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 3208). Outline: Intelligent agents; uninformed and informed search (A*), local and adversarial search; probabilistic reasoning, HMMs; decision theory and MDPs; supervised learning, unsupervised learning (clustering) and reinforcement learning. References: Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach.

items.question: What is Software Testing and Quality Assurance about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3209 Software Testing and Quality Assurance - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 3210). Outline: Test life cycle and methodology; black-box techniques; white-box techniques; reviews and inspections; unit to acceptance testing; test management; quality assurance and metrics; TDD and BDD; tools such as JUnit, Selenium, Apache JMeter and Cucumber. References: Chauhan, Software Testing: Principles and Practices; Myers, Sandler and Badgett, The Art of Software Testing; Crispin and Gregory, Agile Testing.

items.question: Give me the course details of Software Design and Architecture.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3211 Software Design and Architecture - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 3212). Outline: Design process and design model; architectural design (styles, genres, data-flow mapping); component-level design; user interface design (golden rules, interface analysis and design). References: Pressman, Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach, 7th ed.; Sommerville, Software Engineering, 9th ed.

items.question: Details of SE 4100
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 4100 Internship - Year 4 Term 1; 18 credits (lab/practical). Outline: A six-month full-time internship with a company; evaluated by the company's marks plus at least two presentations given at IIT. References: No references listed.

items.question: Tell me everything about the Project course.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 4202 Project - Year 4 Term 2; 6 credits (lab/practical). Outline: A software development or research project; research projects submit a thesis; development projects submit a proposal, SRS, SDS, test plan and user manual; multiple intermediate presentations. References: No references listed.

items.question: What is Software Maintenance about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 4203 Software Maintenance - Year 4 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 4204). Outline: Lifecycle roadmap of evolution and maintenance; evolution laws; pre-delivery and transition models; impact analysis; handling customer problems; retirement; maintainability versus bad smells; refactoring; legacy-system evolution. References: Jarzabek, Effective Software Maintenance and Evolution; Grubb and Takang, Software Maintenance: Concepts and Practice, 2nd ed.

items.question: Give me the course details of Software Project Management.
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 4205 Software Project Management - Year 4 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 4206). Outline: Project management principles; planning and estimation; WBS and scheduling (PERT, CPM, Gantt); managing risk, quality, configuration and change; monitoring and control with earned value; industry scenarios and case studies. References: Stellman and Greene, Applied Software Project Management; Phillips, IT Project Management; Rubin, Essential Scrum.

items.question: Details of CSE 804
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 804 Information Retrieval - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: Boolean retrieval and inverted indexes; tokenization and tolerant retrieval; index construction; tf-idf scoring and the vector space model; evaluation; relevance feedback; language models; enterprise search with Apache Lucene. References: Manning, Raghavan and Schutze, An Introduction to Information Retrieval; McCandless et al., Lucene in Action (2nd ed.).

items.question: Tell me everything about the Data Mining and Warehousing course.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 825 Data Mining and Warehousing - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: Introduction to data mining; knowing and pre-processing data; data warehousing, OLAP and data cubes; frequent patterns; classification and cluster analysis; research trends. References: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques (text book).

items.question: What is Pattern Recognition and Image Processing about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 829 Pattern Recognition and Image Processing - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: Digital image fundamentals; enhancement in the spatial and frequency domains; restoration; colour processing; wavelets; compression; morphology; segmentation; representation; object recognition. References: Gonzalez and Woods, Digital Image Processing.

items.question: Give me the course details of Computer Graphics and Multimedia.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 831 Computer Graphics and Multimedia - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: OpenGL, colour models, geometric transformations, 3D viewing, ray tracing, Phong shading, rasterization (Bresenham), hidden surface removal and texture mapping. References: Foley, van Dam, Feiner and Hughes, Computer Graphics: Principles and Practice.

items.question: Details of BUS 842
items.ground_truth_answer: BUS 842 Strategic Management - elective; 3 credits (3 theory + 0 lab). Outline: Strategic leadership and competitive advantage; industry and environment analysis; functional and business-level strategy; technology and global strategy; strategic software engineering (product lines, effort and cost estimation, software economics). References: Hill and Jones, Theory of Strategic Management (8th ed.); Fred R. David, Strategic Management: Concepts and Cases (12th ed.).

items.question: Tell me everything about the Digital System Design course.
items.ground_truth_answer: EEE 202 Digital System Design - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: Number systems and codes; Boolean algebra; logic gates; combinational design and minimization (K-map, Quine-McCluskey); programmable logic devices; sequential logic design; counters and registers; memory design. References: Nelson et al., Digital Logic Circuit Analysis and Design; Mano and Kime, Logic and Computer Design Fundamentals (4th ed.); Hayes; Tocci et al.; Brown and Vranesic; Dewey.

items.question: What is Data Communication and Networking about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 303 Data Communication and Networking - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: Data communication and network models; physical layer and media; data link layer (error control, MAC protocols, Ethernet, wireless LANs); network-layer logical addressing. References: B. A. Forouzan, Data Communications and Networking, 5th ed.

items.question: Give me the course details of Parallel Computing.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 501 Parallel Computing - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: Parallel computer models; program and network properties; scalable performance (Amdahl's law); pipelining and superscalar techniques; multiprocessors, cache coherence; parallel programming software. References: Kai Hwang, Advanced Computer Architecture; Lin and Snyder, Principles of Parallel Programming; Mattson et al., Patterns for Parallel Programming; Herlihy and Shavit, The Art of Multiprocessor Programming.

items.question: Details of BUS 602
items.ground_truth_answer: BUS 602 Management Information Systems - elective; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab). Outline: Foundations of information systems; IT hardware, software, data and networks; business applications (e-business, ERP, SCM, e-commerce, decision support); development process; security, ethical and global management challenges. References: James O'Brien, Management Information Systems, 10th ed.

items.question: Tell me everything about the Computer, Data and Network Security course.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 802 Computer, Data and Network Security - elective; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab). Outline: Same outline as Information Security: security concepts and attacks, classical encryption, block ciphers, public-key cryptography, hash functions and signatures, key management, network and internet security. References: Stallings, Data and Computer Communications, 8th ed. (2007).

items.question: What is Applied Data Science about? Include credits, term and reference books.
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 844 Applied Data Science - elective; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab). Outline: Data cleaning and publishing; visualization; predictive and Bayesian analytics; classifiers, clustering and association rules; lab on big data, pattern discovery and visualization with Hadoop and TensorFlow. References: Mount and Zumel, Practical Data Science with R (text book); O'Neil and Schutt, Doing Data Science; Jurney, Agile Data Science; Tufte; Witten et al.; Russell, Mining the Social Web.

items.question: Give me details of DBMS-I
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2207 Database Management System-I - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2208). Outline: Introduction to database systems; ER data modelling; relational model and normalization; SQL; overview of object-oriented databases and persistence. References: Silberschatz, Korth and Sudarshan, Database System Concepts, 6th ed.

items.question: Give me the details of Web Tech
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 3103 Web Technology - Year 3 Term 1; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab; lab course CSE 3104). Outline: HTML, JavaScript and CSS; server-side programming (HTTP and application servers, MVC frameworks, web services); database access (ORM, LINQ); web security (DoS, buffer overflow, XSS, authentication and access control). References: Deitel et al., Internet and World Wide Web: How to Program; Rajkamal, Web Technology; Bayross, Teach Yourself Web Technologies; Niederst, Web Design in a Nutshell.

items.question: course details of Numerical Analysis
items.ground_truth_answer: MATH 2107 Numerical Analysis for Engineers - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course MATH 2108). Outline: Calculus review and C programming; sources and propagation of errors; root finding for nonlinear equations; systems of linear equations; interpolation and approximation; numerical integration and differentiation. References: E. Balagurusamy, Numerical Methods (Tata McGraw-Hill, 2002).

items.question: Give me details of the Software Testing course
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3209 Software Testing and Quality Assurance - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 3210). Outline: Test life cycle and methodology; black-box techniques; white-box techniques; reviews and inspections; unit to acceptance testing; test management; quality assurance and metrics; TDD and BDD; tools such as JUnit, Selenium, Apache JMeter and Cucumber. References: Chauhan, Software Testing: Principles and Practices; Myers, Sandler and Badgett, The Art of Software Testing; Crispin and Gregory, Agile Testing.

items.question: Give me details of Intro to Software Engineering
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 1113 Introduction to Software Engineering - Year 1 Term 1; 3 credits (theory). Outline: Introduction to computers, basic computer organization, processor and memory, storage and I/O devices, software, software engineering and software process models. References: Pradip K. Sinha, Computer Fundamentals (BPB); Pressman, Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach, 7th ed.

items.question: details of operating system course
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2201 Operating Systems and System Programming - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2202). Outline: Processes, threads, IPC and scheduling; memory management and virtual memory; file systems; I/O; deadlocks; virtualization and cloud. References: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 7th ed.; Tanenbaum and Bos, Modern Operating Systems, 4th ed.

items.question: Give me details of Computer Networks Lab
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2106 is the lab paired with CSE 2105; it follows the same outline. CSE 2105 Computer Networks - Year 2 Term 1; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2106). Outline: Overview of the Internet and protocol layers; application layer (HTTP, FTP, e-mail, DNS); transport layer (UDP, TCP, congestion control); network layer (IP, subnetting, link-state and distance-vector routing, RIP, OSPF, BGP). References: B. A. Forouzan, Data Communications and Networking, 5th ed.

items.question: Details of Data Structure Lab
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 1202 is the lab paired with CSE 1201; it follows the same outline. CSE 1201 Data Structure - Year 1 Term 2; 3 credits (1 theory + 2 lab; lab course CSE 1202). Outline: Complexity and searching; sorting (insertion, selection, bubble, quick, merge, radix) and recursion; linked lists; stacks and queues with prefix/infix/postfix evaluation; hashing; trees (binary, BST, heaps, Huffman, AVL, B and B+); graphs (BFS, DFS, shortest paths, MST, topological sort); greedy, divide and conquer, dynamic programming and backtracking. References: Schaum's Outline: Data Structures; Horowitz and Sahni, Fundamentals of Data Structures; Robert Kruse, Data Structures and Program Design (2nd ed.).

items.question: Tell me about the Information Security Lab
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 2206 is the lab paired with CSE 2205; it follows the same outline. CSE 2205 Information Security - Year 2 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 2206). Outline: Security concepts and attacks; classical encryption; block ciphers and DES; public-key cryptography (RSA, Diffie-Hellman); hash functions, MACs and digital signatures; key management and X.509; network and internet security (TLS, WLAN, e-mail). References: Mark Stamp, Information Security: Principles and Practice, 2nd ed. (Wiley, 2011).

items.question: What is the Artificial Intelligence Lab course?
items.ground_truth_answer: CSE 3208 is the lab paired with CSE 3207; it follows the same outline. CSE 3207 Artificial Intelligence - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course CSE 3208). Outline: Intelligent agents; uninformed and informed search (A*), local and adversarial search; probabilistic reasoning, HMMs; decision theory and MDPs; supervised learning, unsupervised learning (clustering) and reinforcement learning. References: Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach.

items.question: Details of Software Testing and Quality Assurance Lab
items.ground_truth_answer: SE 3210 is the lab paired with SE 3209; it follows the same outline. SE 3209 Software Testing and Quality Assurance - Year 3 Term 2; 3 credits (2 theory + 1 lab; lab course SE 3210). Outline: Test life cycle and methodology; black-box techniques; white-box techniques; reviews and inspections; unit to acceptance testing; test management; quality assurance and metrics; TDD and BDD; tools such as JUnit, Selenium, Apache JMeter and Cucumber. References: Chauhan, Software Testing: Principles and Practices; Myers, Sandler and Badgett, The Art of Software Testing; Crispin and Gregory, Agile Testing.

items.question: Give me details of Software Project Lab.
items.ground_truth_answer: Two courses match: SE 2112 Software Project Lab I (Year 2 Term 1, 3 credits, individual project) and SE 3112 Software Project Lab II (Year 3 Term 1, 3 credits, team project of 3 with an SRS first). Ask which, or cover both.

items.question: Give me details of Object Oriented Concepts.
items.ground_truth_answer: Two courses match: SE 1213 Object Oriented Concepts I (Year 1 Term 2, 2+1 credits, Java basics, UML, core OO) and SE 2109 Object Oriented Concepts II (Year 2 Term 1, 2+1 credits, SOLID, patterns, advanced Java).

items.question: Details of Probability and Statistics.
items.ground_truth_answer: Two courses match: STAT 1105 Probability and Statistics for Engineers-I (Year 1 Term 1, 3 credits) and STAT 1205 Probability and Statistics for Engineers-II (Year 1 Term 2, 3 credits).

items.question: Give me the details of the Bengali Literature course.
items.ground_truth_answer: GE 1211 Bengali Literature appears only in the Year 1 Term 2 table (3 credits, theory); the handbook gives no outline or references.

items.question: Give me details of the Machine Learning course.
items.ground_truth_answer: There is no course titled Machine Learning. ML topics (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning) appear in CSE 3207 Artificial Intelligence, and the CSE 844 Applied Data Science elective covers classifiers and clustering.

items.question: Give me details of the Compiler Design course.
items.ground_truth_answer: No course named Compiler Design exists in the handbook.

items.question: details of Python Programming course
items.ground_truth_answer: No Python course exists in the handbook (programming languages named: C, Java, R).
